newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Flights improve in West Africa as strike eases.
newsitem.headline: Flights improve in West Africa as strike eases.

text.p: Air travel improved across West Africa on Thursday as air traffic controllers in 15 countries eased a strike over pay that disrupted flights over Christmas, airport officials said.
The stoppage, launched at dawn on Wednesday, had been called off in Abidjan, the regional hub of air travel, and in Dakar, Senegal, as well as the Malian capital Bamako, they said.
Union officials in Cotonou, Benin, said controllers there had agreed to return to work by midday on Thursday.
Aiport officials in Abidjan said services resumed there on Wednesday night, when an Ethiopian Airlines flight left for Addis Ababa.
"All our scheduled flights are operating normally today," an airport duty official told Reuters.
Air traffic controllers in the 15 member states of the Agency for the Safety of Aerial Navigation (ASECNA) launched a 48-hour stoppage to back demands for better pay and conditions.

But strike leaders at the ASECNA workers union headquarters in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, said later the action would be indefinite following the suspension of their chief by the agency's authorities.
"We regret to announce that the radio blackout order will henceforth be observed for an indefinite period until our demands are satisfactorily addressed," said a union statement.
Just about all ASECNA members are former French colonies in West and Central Africa and the Indian Ocean. The union says its members control air space over a 16 million sq km area.

The strike also affected non-Francophone neighouring states, but among the worst hit carriers was Air France which has several flights to the region. More than half a dozen such flights from Paris were cancelled on Christmas Day.
